question: A team applies the same single sign-off step to every Claude-assisted output, from internal meeting notes to a statement that will be filed with a regulator. What is the greatest risk?
options: A) Irreversible, externally visible work gets no more scrutiny than notes nobody will ever act on.
B) Reviewers will refuse the extra workload, so the sign-off step will be abandoned within weeks.
C) Reviewers will start to rely on Claude's wording, and their comments will grow shorter over time.
D) Every output will take equally long to clear, which slows the team's routine work considerably.
correct_answers: A) Irreversible, externally visible work gets no more scrutiny than notes nobody will ever act on.
explanations: Correct. Review effort should scale with consequence and reversibility. A uniform step spends the same attention everywhere, which leaves the rare high-blast-radius output under-examined.
Incorrect. Workload may become a problem, but the immediate exposure is that the process cannot tell important work from routine work.
Incorrect. Review fatigue is real, but it is a consequence of the flat process rather than the central danger it creates.
Incorrect. Slower routine work is an efficiency cost. The serious risk sits at the other end of the range, on the filings.
